short: Germany's last gamble in the west, launched before American manpower could arrive.
full:
Russia's collapse released some fifty veteran divisions for the Western Front, and Ludendorff meant to use them before the Americans arrived in strength. Operation Michael opened on 21 March 1918 with a five-hour hurricane bombardment from over 6,000 guns, followed by stormtroops trained to infiltrate past strongpoints rather than assault them head-on. The British Fifth Army was broken and the line fell back forty miles, the largest movement in the west since 1914.

Three further offensives followed, in Flanders, on the Aisne and towards Reims. The Germans reached the Marne again and shelled Paris with railway guns, but they had no cavalry or motor transport to exploit the gaps, and they were advancing into ground they had themselves devastated in 1917. Around a million casualties bought territory of no strategic value and stretched an already thin line. On 18 July the French counterattacked at Soissons, and the initiative passed to the Allies for the rest of the war.
